<!-- Generated by tools/copilot/sync.py from .claude/commands/start.md; edit the source and rerun it. -->
Start or continue a report (the main flow, docs/design/phase1-usability.md Part A): the text after /kit-start in my message
Follow this whenever someone asks for a dashboard or report; nobody needs to type this command. Talk only in
docs/PLAIN-WORDS.md words: no slash commands, paths, commands, flags, IDs or JSON; after every step one line saying
what happens next. Run every pbik command with `--report json` and answer from its facts, needs and next. Mark each
stage with `pbik step start|end <stage>` and every reply from the person or approval window with
`pbik step note <what> --interaction` (a window: `window: <title>`).

Never wait in silence: before any step that can take longer than 30 seconds (the plan picture, opening Desktop, a
large build), say in one line what it is; run it so its "Still ..." lines reach you (in the background, reading its
output) and pass one on at least every minute ("Still drawing the plan picture (1 min so far)."). If a step fails, say
the plain reason it gives; never leave a reply empty.

## 0. Where are we (one folder = one project)
Run `pbik status`. In a project, say its line ("You're past the plan picture; next is the colours") and carry on from
there. In a fresh copy of the kit, make this folder the project: `pbik project setup` (data class restricted unless
the person said otherwise; the folder's name unless they gave one) and say its lines: the project's name and its two
folders, Model and Reference. In the master kit, say its line (copy the kit to a new folder, open that, ask there)
and stop: never build in the master kit. No projects subfolder, no second folder, no chat switch.

## 1. Start (stage "start")
1. `pbik start check`, at the start of every build: one line for each folder, what it holds and what is missing,
   and pass them on as they are. Never open File Explorer. If something is missing, ask the person to put a copy in
   the named folder (Model: the semantic model export; Reference: a wireframe, screenshots, requirements or an
   existing report's folder), then say done. A picture pasted in the chat: read it there.
2. `pbik start detect`: it names the path. Say what you got in one line. Never read a refused file. With Reference
   empty: ask the one open question ("What should this report help people decide?") and offer the starter layouts.
3. The model: `pbik model intake` (it reads the Model folder, deleting data files first). Say its grouped lines. A model approved before is recognised (no approval needed). Otherwise
   the items that need the person are the only model questions; then prepare and open the approval window
   (`pbik gate prepare synth-approve`, `pbik gate open synth-approve`, `pbik gate wait synth-approve`). Mark stage
   "model" done (`pbik status --done model`).
4. Build option: `pbik mode` gives the default and any suggestion. Ask only if there is no default yet, in one line
   with both descriptions (PLAIN-WORDS "Build options"), batched with any other question. Record it (`pbik mode
   guided|quick`). They can switch any time ("switch to guided", "finish the rest quickly"): record it and go on.
5. The path:
   - from report: `pbik layout from-report <the .Report folder in the inputs> --out design/specs/layout.json`
   - from wireframe or picture: design/scripts/ref_layout.py (an image: write its boxes file first), into
     design/specs/layout.json
   - starter layouts: ask "What should this report help people decide?" (with requirements, take the answer from
     them and don't ask). Then `pbik start starters --kpi <measure> ... --date <field> --category <field>` with names
     from the model, draw each (`pbik plan picture design/specs/starters/<name>.layout.json --out
     design/plan/starters/<name>`), show the 2-3 pictures and let them pick one and adjust it in plain words; copy the
     pick to design/specs/layout.json.
   Mark "start" done.

## 2. Plan as a picture (stages "page purpose" and "plan")
1. Fill what the layout needs (bindings from the model, alt text, build reasons; tokens and theme as /plan does),
   choosing defaults for everything only the person doesn't need to decide: which total measure, colour rules,
   default filters. Each default goes in the list as an assumption (`--assume`). Every headline number needs a
   comparison. A fallback (CLAUDE.md "Native first") goes in the list with the native option tried.
2. `pbik plan show --purpose "P1=<what the page helps decide>" --assume "..."` (pass every assumption each time: the
   list replaces the last one). The picture is the fast preview: the theme, tokens and the templates' look with
   example values (never data). Show the pictures: in the Claude desktop app in the chat; in VS Code (Copilot or
   Claude Code) `pbik plan open` opens them beside the chat. Give the short list from design/plan/plan.md in plain
   words. If it lists a text too faint to read, fix it in layout.json and show the plan again before asking for the OK.
3. Guided build: stop after the page purpose and after the plan for an OK. Quick build: this is the only stop.
4. Changes in plain words: update layout.json or the plan, show it again. On OK: `pbik plan approve`.

## 3. Build (stages "theme", "build", "checks", "polish", "result")
Run `pbik project check` first: if it says Desktop changed since the kit was last tested, run the after-update
checks without asking (record the version, `pbik schemas support --refresh`, the regression suite, a changelog row in
VERSIONS.md) and list the Desktop smoke test as not done yet in the result. Run `pbik plan check`: it fails only when
what the person approved changed (which visuals, what they show, where they sit); the kit's own fixes and polish
after the OK (a taller slicer, number formats, column widths, a legend) need no new OK, so never stop for them in a
quick build; list them in the result. If it fails, show the plan again. Then, as /theme, /build, /review and /fix
do (their files say how), with a check after each step and one fix and recheck when a check fails:
- theme (the colours); build (`pbik build "<project name>" design/specs/layout.json`: the first build makes a clean,
  empty report folder itself; never copy another report); checks (`pbik validate`, audit_layout.py, audit_ids.py);
- before screenshots: open the report in Desktop (`pbik desktop open`: it waits until Desktop answers, saying "still
  opening" meanwhile), reload (`pbik desktop reload`), screenshot
  each page (`pbik desktop screenshot`); polish: up to two rounds of review and fix against the approved picture and
  design/checks.md; after screenshots. Before a reload after your own edits: `pbik desktop close`; if it leaves
  Desktop open, ask the person to close it without saving and wait.
- Guided build: stop after each stage, show what changed, wait for an OK. Quick build: don't stop, except when
  unsure: a check still failing after its fix, a fallback not in the plan, a measure the plan didn't name, two
  measures that fit one KPI, an approval window, a Desktop or bridge failure. Then ask one plain question with the
  default you would take.
- The kit does these itself, without asking: months sort by month number (the made-up model gets the sort-by column;
  a live model: say why not and give the Desktop clicks), number columns' headers right-aligned, thousands
  separators in the made-up model's number formats.
- Score: `pbik score --item 1=<your own judgment of the screenshots against the approved picture> --item 3=<every
  card's measure returns a value: DAX query> --item 7=<slicers filter, buttons go where they should> --final`.
Result: the before and after screenshots (shown or opened as the plan pictures), the polish score, and what you
couldn't fix with its Desktop click steps (design/known-gaps.md). Then offer "Switch to live?": with a person's yes,
prepare and open the window (`pbik gate prepare bind-live --from picked` after the Desktop model pick, or from the
pack), and wait.

## 4. Wrap-up
Ask once, optionally: "How many minutes did you spend tidying it in Desktop?" (`pbik score --hand-minutes N`).
Then as /wrapup does, with the polish score and the page purpose.
